title: orobanche alba subsp. major
intro: Orobanche alba subsp. major, commonly known as White Broomrape, is a parasitic flowering plant of the family Orobanchaceae, which obtains its nutrients by connecting to the roots of its host plant, typically legumes. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and antimicrobial properties, which may help to treat various conditions such as wounds, infections, and digestive issues. The therapeutic actions of White Broomrape include stimulating digestion, reducing fever, and alleviating pain. The bioactive constituents of this plant include alkaloids, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
